shelves.title: Meaning, wonder & spiritual curiosity
shelves.intro: A conversation or a reflective question can be a useful beginning. Explore different approaches to meaning at your own pace.
shelves.orientation: Meaning is not only a subject to read about. It can also be a way of paying attention to a familiar activity, a person, or an unanswered question. These selections offer conversations, context, and reflective invitations rather than a single account of how life should be lived.
shelves.approach: Begin with a format you enjoy. A conversation lets you hear how someone arrives at a view; a contextual introduction helps explain unfamiliar language; a reflective question leaves room for your own response. Keep the experience of finding something meaningful separate from accepting every explanation offered for it.

shelves.title: Attention, presence & self-kindness
shelves.intro: Free recordings and optional practices for approaching an ordinary moment with a little more attention.
shelves.orientation: A practice can be small enough to fit the day you actually have. The resources here differ in style, tradition, and format, so start by choosing something understandable rather than trying to compare every possible benefit. A short recording or an outward-looking exercise is a complete starting point.
shelves.approach: The practice descriptions are not treatment recommendations or evidence that one program suits everyone. Adapt or stop an exercise that feels unhelpful, preserve accessibility and care needs, and use appropriate human support for significant difficulties. You can also explore attention through a poem or an ordinary conversation.

shelves.title: AI literacy & thoughtful use
shelves.intro: Understand the tools well enough to ask useful questions, check an answer, and decide when a simpler approach is sufficient.
shelves.orientation: Learning about AI need not mean following every product announcement. A useful foundation is to understand what a system is being asked to do, what information it receives, and what you will need to check. These resources offer accessible explanations and optional routes into deeper study.
shelves.approach: Independent educational material and vendor-authored tutorials serve different purposes. Read product examples as examples of the provider’s approach, not as neutral comparisons. Free lessons can demonstrate features that require payment elsewhere. Use fictional or non-sensitive material while learning, and keep responsibility for consequential decisions.

shelves.title: Nature, science & everyday wonder
shelves.intro: Explore a familiar bird, the night sky, an ocean question, or a hands-on explanation of something you have noticed.
shelves.orientation: Wonder does not need an exotic setting. An unfamiliar sound, a shadow, or a question about water can open a satisfying line of inquiry. This collection brings together observation aids, scientific explanations, and visual tools that help curiosity move beyond the screen.
shelves.approach: Use identification and visualization tools as learning aids, not as guarantees about the world in front of you. Keep safe distances from wildlife, do not use an identification guess to decide what to eat, and follow activity-specific safety instructions. A text explanation or an indoor observation is just as valid a route as an outing.

shelves.title: Relationships, memory & listening
shelves.intro: Questions and practical resources for listening carefully, preserving a story, and making participation easier.
shelves.orientation: A useful resource can make it easier to begin a conversation or keep an agreed memory accessible. It cannot decide what another person wants to share. Start with an invitation, listen to the answer, and choose an activity that respects everyone involved.
shelves.approach: Recording, uploading, editing, and publishing are separate decisions. Ask about each relevant use rather than assuming that a friendly conversation grants blanket permission. Some people will prefer a private, unrecorded exchange. For technology-supported assistance, follow the provider’s safety and privacy guidance and the preferences of the person receiving help.

shelves.title: Philosophy, decisions & perspective
shelves.intro: Readable introductions and small models for examining an idea, comparing interpretations, and thinking through a choice.
shelves.orientation: A clear explanation can help you notice an assumption you had not considered. Philosophy offers arguments to examine, while a model makes selected relationships easier to see. Neither requires treating life as a puzzle with one hidden correct answer.
shelves.approach: Begin with an introductory passage or one interactive example. Ask what the argument assumes, what the model leaves out, and whether its conclusions fit the question you actually have. A useful analogy can illuminate a decision without reducing relationships or personal values to a numerical score.

shelves.title: Wisdom traditions & religious literacy
shelves.intro: Encounter particular traditions in context, alongside tools for understanding religious diversity and interpretation.
shelves.orientation: Spiritual curiosity can become more respectful when it learns the context of the words it borrows. These starting points include academic orientation and resources produced within particular traditions. They are different kinds of reading, and their perspectives are identified rather than blended into universal advice.
shelves.approach: This is a selective introduction, not a complete map of religions or a statement of Nolan’s religious identity. Traditions contain internal differences, and translations involve interpretation. Read introductory context before extracting a quotation or practice. Inclusion makes a resource available for exploration; it does not imply affiliation or agreement with every teaching.

shelves.title: Free learning & practical understanding
shelves.intro: Build a little understanding through open lessons, course materials, textbooks, and visual demonstrations.
shelves.orientation: You can learn one useful thing without enrolling in a complete program. Choose a question you would like to answer, then match the resource to the size of that question. A plain tutorial may be more useful today than a university lecture series, while a textbook can provide a reference to return to.
shelves.approach: Open materials are not automatically current in every detail, and access to a course is not the same as enrollment for academic credit. Check the level, date, and any account requirements. After reading, explain one idea in your own words or try one low-stakes example before moving on.

shelves.title: Books, art & creative exploration
shelves.intro: Find something to read, hear, look at, or make, without needing to turn the encounter into an achievement.
shelves.orientation: Creative work gives attention somewhere to go. You might spend a few minutes with a poem, compare two artworks, listen to a story, or make a simple rhythm. The point is not to complete a cultural checklist; it is to encounter something that holds your interest.
shelves.approach: Free access and permission to reuse are different. Read the rights information attached to an item before copying it into your own work. Older books may contain dated assumptions or language, and a digital collection represents editorial choices rather than a complete history. Enjoying a work does not require adopting all of its author’s views.

shelves.title: Digital privacy & confident use
shelves.intro: Understand everyday settings, recognize suspicious requests, and keep the tools you use aligned with your needs.
shelves.orientation: Digital confidence comes from a few understandable choices, not from making every possible adjustment. Start with the device or account you already use and the specific concern you are trying to address. Official instructions and independent explanations can help you distinguish a meaningful setting from an impressive-sounding promise.
shelves.approach: These links provide education, not a security audit of your devices. Provider guidance is specific to its products, and settings can change. Preserve recovery options and essential access before changing an account. Never paste passwords, recovery codes, or private records into a public exercise or an AI conversation.

shelves.title: Useful tools & everyday skills
shelves.intro: Free core tools and readable guides for notes, documents, sources, audio, maps, and small practical tasks.
shelves.orientation: Start with a task rather than a tool collection. A document that opens reliably, a note you can find again, or a clear recording may be all you need. The selections here offer free core functions or free instructions, with installation, optional services, and practical limits identified.
shelves.approach: Choose official download routes and review the current requirements before installing anything. Keep backups when changing a working process, and test a non-sensitive example first. A free application can offer paid storage or services; a free repair guide does not make equipment free or a hazardous repair safe to attempt.

shelves.title: Community, access & contribution
shelves.intro: Small ways to contribute attention or skills to shared knowledge, public collections, and community projects.
shelves.orientation: A meaningful use of technology can benefit someone other than the person operating it. These projects offer ways to help preserve public material, contribute to research, or explore a defined volunteer role. Start by understanding the task and the people it is intended to serve.
shelves.approach: Contribution is not a test of personal worth. Read the instructions, training, privacy rules, and time commitments before joining. A short careful contribution can be more helpful than a large inaccurate one. Opportunities may require registration or selection, and a listing does not guarantee placement or payment.

resources.why: A way to understand an artwork through materials, history, and context rather than only a quick visual impression.
resources.start: Open one essay on a medium or period that catches your attention.
resources.limit: The museum’s scholarship is a perspective on its collections; check separate permissions before reusing images or text.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Learning Music
resources.creator: Ableton
resources.requirements: Free browser lessons. JavaScript and audio are needed; no Ableton software purchase is required.
resources.why: A playful route into rhythm and musical structure that lets you make something small while learning.
resources.start: Start with the opening beat activity and change a pattern.
resources.limit: Vendor-created education; this is not a recommendation to buy its production software.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.
resources.perspective: Creative education from a software provider

resources.title: Poetry Foundation: poems
resources.creator: Poetry Foundation
resources.requirements: The selected web poems are publicly readable; books, print subscriptions, and reuse permissions are separate.
resources.why: A broad starting point for finding a poem by theme or poet without needing to turn the reading into a lesson.
resources.start: Choose one poem and read it before looking for a summary or interpretation.
resources.limit: Free reading is not permission to reproduce a poem. The collection includes many distinct perspectives.
resources.review_scope: Official indexed poems-page description reviewed. Direct retrieval was restricted in the research browser; individual poem pages were not tested.

resources.title: Surveillance Self-Defense
resources.creator: Electronic Frontier Foundation
resources.requirements: The guides are free to read. Tools discussed may have separate setup requirements.
resources.why: A practical framework for choosing a few security habits that fit the information and relationships you want to protect.
resources.start: Begin with the Basics section or the guide to making a security plan.
resources.limit: A digital-rights organization’s guidance, not a guarantee that a product or device is secure.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Firefox tracking-protection guide
resources.creator: Mozilla Support
resources.requirements: Free support article. Its settings apply to Firefox, not every browser or device.
resources.why: A specific explanation of a browser setting, useful for making an informed choice instead of installing another privacy tool by default.
resources.start: Read the description of the protection levels and their possible effects on websites.
resources.limit: Settings and behavior can change with browser versions; stronger restrictions can affect site functions.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Recognizing scams
resources.creator: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
resources.requirements: Free U.S. consumer-information articles; no account required to read.
resources.why: Clear examples of suspicious requests can help a reader pause and verify a message before acting.
resources.start: Choose an article relevant to a type of message you encounter, rather than reading every alert.
resources.limit: Reporting and remedies are U.S.-specific. This directory is not legal advice or a personalized fraud assessment.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Personal Safety User Guide
resources.creator: Apple Support
resources.requirements: The guide is free to read. Features depend on the Apple device and software version.
resources.why: A reference for understanding what information is shared through a device and which controls are available.
resources.start: Use the contents to find the sharing or account feature you want to understand.
resources.limit: In a coercive or unsafe situation, changing settings can have consequences; follow the guide’s safety context and seek suitable support.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Google Safety Center
resources.creator: Google
resources.requirements: Public explanations are free to browse. Applying account controls requires access to your own account.
resources.why: A place to understand Google’s account and safety controls through its own documentation rather than a third-party checklist.
resources.start: Choose one account-protection topic and compare it with your current setup.
resources.limit: Vendor information is not an independent privacy audit or a comparison with other services.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Stories of Web Users
resources.creator: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative
resources.requirements: Free public stories and accessibility explanations.
resources.why: Concrete examples of different access needs can make technology discussions more attentive to people rather than only features.
resources.start: Read one user story and notice which design choice helps or prevents participation.
resources.limit: Illustrative stories do not represent every person with a disability; ask about individual preferences.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: LibreOffice
resources.creator: The Document Foundation
resources.requirements: Free, open-source desktop office suite. Installation is required; optional support services are separate.
resources.why: A full document toolkit for readers who need ordinary office tasks without a recurring software subscription.
resources.start: Read the system requirements and try a non-sensitive document from an official download.
resources.limit: File compatibility can vary. Keep an original copy when trying another application.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Joplin
resources.creator: Joplin project
resources.requirements: The note-taking apps are free and open source. Joplin Cloud and some services are paid options.
resources.why: A possible home for notes that need to remain understandable and portable, without building a complicated personal dashboard.
resources.start: Read the app and synchronization options, then try one small notebook.
resources.limit: Sync, backup, and encryption choices need deliberate setup; free software is not a blanket privacy guarantee.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Zotero
resources.creator: Corporation for Digital Scholarship
resources.requirements: The core research application is free. Additional hosted file storage is an optional paid service.
resources.why: A practical way to keep the source behind an interesting idea so it can be found and checked again.
resources.start: Save one public article and inspect its title, author, and link for accuracy.
resources.limit: Automatically captured metadata needs checking; the tool does not establish that a source is reliable.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Audacity
resources.creator: Audacity project
resources.requirements: The core audio editor is free and open source. Installation is required; additional services have separate terms.
resources.why: A useful option for making a clear recording or editing an agreed conversation without building a full production setup.
resources.start: Use the official download and manual, then test a short recording of your own voice.
resources.limit: Permission to record and permission to publish remain separate. Keep an unedited original.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: OpenStreetMap
resources.creator: OpenStreetMap contributors and Foundation
resources.requirements: The map is free to browse. An account is needed to contribute edits; other map services set their own terms.
resources.why: An example of shared knowledge made useful through technology, with ordinary places and paths as a starting point.
resources.start: Explore a familiar area and compare the map with information you can independently verify.
resources.limit: Community data can be incomplete or outdated. A map is not proof of access rights, safe conditions, or opening times.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: iFixit repair guides
resources.creator: iFixit and its contributors
resources.requirements: The step-by-step guides are free to read. Tools, parts, and optional services are not necessarily free.
resources.why: A reminder that a useful technology decision can involve understanding and maintaining something rather than replacing it.
resources.start: Browse a low-risk clothing or household guide and read every step before deciding whether to attempt it.
resources.limit: Match the exact item and your skills. Hazardous, electrical, battery, medical, or other safety-critical work can require qualified help.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.
resources.perspective: Repair education from a commercial provider

resources.title: Smithsonian Transcription Center
resources.creator: Smithsonian Institution
resources.requirements: Public project information is free to browse. Individual contribution workflows may require an account.
resources.why: A route into helping public collections become easier to search and read, starting with the project’s own instructions.
resources.start: Read the getting-started instructions, then choose a document and follow the project’s transcription rules.
resources.limit: Contribution interfaces and registration requirements vary; no placement or completed contribution is claimed.
resources.review_scope: Official indexed instructions and FAQ descriptions reviewed. Direct retrieval was unavailable in the research browser; account and contribution workflows were not tested.

resources.title: By the People
resources.creator: Library of Congress
resources.requirements: The introduction is free. Transcription can be done without registration; reviewing and tracking use an account.
resources.why: A small, concrete way to help make historical documents easier for other readers to find and use.
resources.start: Read the introduction and transcription instructions before choosing a page.
resources.limit: The linked introduction explains the service; the contribution interface was not tested in this review.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Zooniverse
resources.creator: Zooniverse research teams and volunteers
resources.requirements: Projects and tutorials are public. Participation and account requirements depend on the project.
resources.why: A way to contribute careful observations to a defined research project rather than simply consuming more information.
resources.start: Choose one project and read its purpose and tutorial before classifying anything.
resources.limit: A volunteer classification is one contribution to a research process, not an independent scientific result.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Distributed Proofreaders
resources.creator: Distributed Proofreaders Foundation
resources.requirements: The walkthrough is public. Register for free to contribute proofreading or other volunteer work.
resources.why: A task that connects close reading with making older books more accessible to other people.
resources.start: Try the public walkthrough before registering or choosing a project.
resources.limit: Follow the project’s formatting and review process; service-hour certification is not generally provided.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Online volunteering
resources.creator: United Nations Volunteers
resources.requirements: Browse the information free; applications require platform registration and meeting the assignment’s criteria.
resources.why: A route for exploring whether a specific skill could be useful to an organization with a defined task.
resources.start: Read the eligibility and commitment information before considering an assignment.
resources.limit: Online assignments are unpaid and selection is not guaranteed. They differ from employed or on-site UN roles.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Missing Maps
resources.creator: Missing Maps partner organizations
resources.requirements: Free public instructions. Mapping contributions typically need an OpenStreetMap account and training.
resources.why: An example of digital work supporting humanitarian information needs through a shared, reviewable process.
resources.start: Read how the project works, then choose a beginner training route rather than immediately editing.
resources.limit: Respect privacy and mapping instructions; accuracy and responsible review matter more than contribution volume.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: NASA Eyes
resources.creator: NASA
resources.requirements: Free browser visualizations. A supported browser and suitable graphics capability are needed.
resources.why: A way to connect an abstract idea about Earth or the solar system with a visual model you can explore.
resources.start: Choose one visualization from the NASA introduction and read what its model represents.
resources.limit: Visualizations are models with specific data and assumptions, not direct views of everything shown.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Astronomy Picture of the Day
resources.creator: NASA and APOD editors
resources.entry_title: Explore Astronomy Picture of the Day
resources.requirements: Public images and explanations are free to read. Image reuse rights vary by credit.
resources.why: An appealing small encounter with astronomy: one image, its context, and a question to investigate further.
resources.start: Look at the featured image, then read the explanation and image credit.
resources.limit: Check image-specific permissions; an image’s visual impact is not evidence for a spiritual interpretation.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Smithsonian Ocean
resources.creator: Smithsonian Institution
resources.requirements: Public articles, features, and learning material are free to browse.
resources.why: A route from curiosity about water and marine life to explanations with more context than a short identification result.
resources.start: Choose a topic under ocean life or ecosystems and begin with one introductory article.
resources.limit: Educational material is not advice for handling wildlife, diving, or making other safety-critical decisions.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Science Snacks
resources.creator: Exploratorium
resources.requirements: Activity instructions are free to browse; materials can cost money.
resources.why: Short activities invite you to examine a familiar phenomenon instead of only reading an explanation of it.
resources.start: Select a simple activity using materials you already have, and read its full instructions and cautions.
resources.limit: Choose an activity suited to your setting and access needs. Read the full safety guidance before handling tools or materials.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: HHMI BioInteractive
resources.creator: Howard Hughes Medical Institute
resources.requirements: Core resources are free; educator-community features require an account and can require verification.
resources.why: Films, explanations, and activities offer a route into how living systems work and how scientific questions are investigated.
resources.start: Choose a short public film or introductory resource rather than an entire classroom sequence.
resources.limit: Designed largely for education; research stories are not personalized health advice.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.

resources.title: Stellarium Web
resources.creator: Stellarium Labs
resources.requirements: Free browser star map. JavaScript is required; desktop and mobile products have separate offerings.
resources.why: An example of a focused digital tool supporting an ordinary question about the sky rather than demanding prolonged attention.
resources.start: Explore the map for a chosen location and time; check the settings before interpreting it.
resources.limit: A simulation is not a weather report or a guarantee of visibility. Never look at the Sun through unfiltered optics.
resources.review_scope: Public provider description and source information reviewed. Registration, app installation, media playback, and completion were not tested.
